prompt: In a reactive form, where does the form's model live?

choices.text: In the template, built from the `<input>` elements
choices.why: The template only points at the model.

choices.text: In the component's class
choices.why: Right. It can be read and typed without a template.

choices.text: In the browser's own form state, read on submit
choices.why: Angular keeps its own model and the input in step with it.

choices.text: In a service the form provides
choices.why: Nothing is provided; the controls are fields of the class.

prompt: The minutes field was emptied. What did the control hold?

choices.why: An empty number field gives no number at all.

choices.text: `''`, an empty string
choices.why: The number field's directive gives numbers, or nothing.

choices.text: `null`
choices.why: Right. That is why the type is `number | null`.

choices.text: `30`, its first value
choices.why: That is what `reset()` gives a `nonNullable` control, not an empty field.

prompt: What does `{ nonNullable: true }` change about `new FormControl(30, ...)`?

choices.text: `reset()` gives 30, not `null`
choices.why: Right. The empty field can still put a `null` there at run time.

choices.text: The input refuses to be emptied
choices.why: The browser lets the person empty it; the control gets `null`.

choices.text: The control becomes invalid when empty
choices.why: Validity is lesson 15, and it needs a validator.

choices.text: The control can no longer be reset
choices.why: It can; it resets to 30.

prompt: A lone control is bound to an input with `<input [___]="minutes" />`.

choices.text: `minutes` is a string in a date form
choices.why: `minutes` is a number; the problem was that it might be missing.

choices.text: `form.value` is not available outside the template
choices.why: It is, and its type is the issue.

choices.text: Each field of `form.value` is optional
choices.why: Right. `getRawValue()` has every field.

choices.text: The group was not given a type argument
choices.why: The type was worked out from the controls.

prompt: Match each binding with the element it goes on.

pairs.right: an element wrapping the array's inputs
an input bound to a lone control

prompt: What does a date input give its control, whatever the browser shows?

choices.text: A `Date` object
choices.why: It gives a string.

choices.text: A string like `2026-10-26`
choices.why: Right. The form the API wants.

choices.text: The day as the person's locale writes it
choices.why: That is only what is on the screen.

choices.text: A number of milliseconds
choices.why: That is `valueAsNumber`, which the directive does not use.

prompt: Why does `add` wait for the server instead of adding the session at once, as `toggle` does?

choices.text: `httpResource` does not allow adding to its value
choices.why: `update` adds to it, once the answer is in.

choices.text: A `POST` is slower than a `PATCH`
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: It has no id until the server answers
choices.why: Right. The store adds the session from the answer.

choices.text: Optimistic updates are not allowed in forms
choices.why: Nothing forbids them; there is no id to show yet.

prompt: What does `(ngSubmit)` on the `<form>` do that a click handler on the button would not?

choices.text: It validates every field first
choices.why: Validation is lesson 15, and `ngSubmit` fires either way.

choices.text: It fires on Enter too, and stops a reload
choices.why: Right. A real form, with keyboard behaviour built in.

choices.text: It sends the form to the server by itself
choices.why: The component's `submit()` does that, through the store.

choices.text: It resets the form after sending
choices.why: The component resets it, when the server has answered.

prompt: Clicking Add with no date brought back `Not added: date must be YYYY-MM-DD`. What does that say about the form?

choices.text: The form is broken and must not send empty fields
choices.why: The form works; it just checks nothing yet.

choices.text: The server should accept an empty date
choices.why: The server is right to refuse it.

choices.text: The error came from the browser
choices.why: The sentence is the API's own.

choices.text: Only the server checked the date, after a round trip
choices.why: Right. Lesson 15 checks before sending, and the server keeps its check.

choices.text: A group whose controls accept `null`
choices.why: The non-nullable builder makes every control non-nullable.

choices.text: An untyped group, since the values are plain
choices.why: The type is worked out from the values, as before.

choices.text: The same group, shorter
choices.why: Right. Two controls, a string and a number, not nullable.

choices.text: A group bound to the template on its own
choices.why: `[formGroup]` still binds it.

prompt: What does a `FormArray` give that a `FormGroup` does not?

choices.text: Controls that are validated together
choices.why: A group's controls are validated together too.

choices.text: A value that is always a string
choices.why: Its value is a list of whatever its controls hold.

choices.text: A length that changes
choices.why: Right. Controls are pushed and removed by position.

choices.text: Controls that need no template
choices.why: Each still needs an input bound to it.

prompt: Why does `startAgain()` clear the array and add one date before calling `reset()`?

choices.text: `reset()` throws on an array with more than one control
choices.why: It works on any array.

choices.text: `reset()` resets values, not structure
choices.why: Right. Three dates would stay three empty dates.

choices.text: The server needs the array cleared to accept the next `POST`
choices.why: The server never sees the form.

choices.text: `clear()` is what sends the requests
choices.why: `submit()` sends them, through the store.

prompt: Why `concatMap` for the `POST`s rather than sending them all at once?

choices.text: `HttpClient` can only have one request out at a time
choices.why: It can have many; `forkJoin` would send them together.

choices.text: They arrive in the order typed
choices.why: Right. The ids come out in that order too.

choices.text: `concatMap` retries a failed one
choices.why: Nothing retries a `POST` here, on purpose.

choices.text: The API refuses two requests in the same second
choices.why: It accepts every valid request.

prompt: The form had two dates and 30 minutes when Add was clicked. How many sessions did that add?
You open a form written for Angular 13 and see `UntypedFormGroup`. What is it?

choices.text: A newer, faster `FormGroup`
choices.why: It is the old behaviour, renamed.

choices.text: A group with validation turned off
choices.why: Validation works the same; only the types are missing.

choices.text: The pre-14 group, renamed
choices.why: Right. Every value is `any`.

choices.text: A Signal Forms group
choices.why: Signal Forms live in `@angular/forms/signals` and are new in Angular 21.

prompt: A form sends `{ ...this.form.value, courseId }` to `store.add`, and the build fails. What is the smallest fix?

choices.text: Cast it with `as Omit<Session, 'id' | 'done'>`
choices.why: That silences the check and keeps the possible `undefined`.

choices.text: Spread `getRawValue()` instead of `value`
choices.why: Right. Every field is in it, so the draft is complete.

choices.text: Make every field of `Session` optional
choices.why: That would weaken every other use of `Session`.

choices.text: Switch to `UntypedFormGroup`
choices.why: That makes the error go away by making everything `any`.
